scaling: Per category: Leads_cat(IS_t) = MainConv_actual * Leads(IS_t)/Leads(IS_current); CPL_cat(IS_t) = CPA_actual * CPL(IS_t)/CPL(IS_current). IS_current = Actuals!Y (rounded integer percent).

master_tables.note: Authoritative master curves as USED by the workbook run: pasted literals in Ratios!A11:A110 (leads) / B11:B110 (CPL), verified identical to the cached grid numerator rows. They differ from the sheet's current parametric formulas beyond IS~59: the production tables hold both curves flat once CPL (at 2dp) stops rising (monotone cap). Golden tests MUST use these tables, not the parametric form.

score_quirk.note: Three workbook integrity quirks the golden test reproduces via overrides (the engine itself implements only the consistent formulas): (1) *0.25 factor on each region's FIRST row (sheet rows 3/10/17/23) for all four score variants — formula drift, absent on all other rows. (2) Opportunity Scores rows 11-12: input columns shifted one row vs Actuals (row 11 carries CP's inputs, row 12 carries NB BRAKES'), so those two scores were computed from the wrong cells' data. (3) Budget Allocation I5 and I12 are broken references (='Recommendation 2'!D6/D13 instead of D5/D12) — the allocator consumed the NEXT row's score for AZ and CO NB BRAKES T2. Consequence: allocation input (BA col I) and the Recommendation sheet's displayed score column disagree on those rows; the golden test asserts against BA col I, the vector the production allocation actually used.
